Szabolcs Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Petőfi út 30, Hungary

Not demolished. This record contains a contradiction worth flagging: it is categorized as demolished, yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'no.' This cemetery sits on the grounds of an ancient hillfort dating to the era of the Pannonian Avars (9th–10th century); a municipal cemetery once also occupied the site, and some Christian gravestones remain, with the Jewish cemetery's perimeter still clearly visible. It was established as early as 1870, per that year's cadastral map, and destroyed at an unknown time; according to a local museum employee cited by izraelitatemetok.hu, its tombstones were transferred to Tokaj. The Jewish population of Szabolcs peaked at 25 in 1880, and by 1941 no Jews remained in the village.
